card.name: Words introducing a span of time
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as 'to', 'through', 'at' or 'of' that come right before a duration or time span, as in 'up to 24 hours' or 'continue treatment through the winter'.

modes.label: Up to a limit
modes.description: The word 'to' after 'up' before a time or amount limit.
modes.example: protected from light for up<< to>> 24 hours prior to preparation of

modes.label: Through a period
modes.description: The word 'through' after a verb, before a named period or season.
modes.example: AD, initiate bupropion hydrochloride extended-release tablets (XL) in the autumn, prior to the onset of depressive symptoms. Continue treatment<< through>> the winter season.

modes.label: Standing or lasting
modes.description: Linking words after a state or action that continues over time, before a duration phrase.
modes.example: precipitate might form: this will dissolve again after the solution is allowed to stand<< at>> room temperature.

card.writes: It seems to lower the chance of long-duration words such as years, weeks and decades coming next.
card.plain: It fires on small words that lead into how long something lasts, like 'up to' or 'through'.
